objective.text: Recognize that adding an index has write and storage costs as well as possible read benefits.

difficulty.rationale: Evaluate an index against both the read path it helps and the write workload it must maintain.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: A PostgreSQL table receives frequent writes. A candidate index improves one report in a representative query plan.

stem: Which additional evidence is most useful before accepting the index for production?

options.text: Whether every model has at least the same number of indexes.
options.rationale: Uniform index counts are not a workload-based justification for this index.
options.misconception: Uniform index counts are not a workload-based justification for this index.

options.text: Whether one cached report response is fast after the index is created.
options.rationale: A cache hit need not exercise the indexed query or expose write costs.
options.misconception: A cache hit need not exercise the indexed query or expose write costs.

options.text: Its effect on write latency, storage and the overall representative workload.
options.rationale: An index can improve a read while imposing maintenance and storage costs elsewhere; the full workload determines the tradeoff.

options.text: Whether the Laravel migration file contains fewer lines after adding the index.
options.rationale: Migration source length does not measure the database workload tradeoff.
options.misconception: Migration source length does not measure the database workload tradeoff.
